This notebook checks the project folders and lists the available source files.
It does not clean, filter, merge, or convert datasets when knitted.

```{r setup, include=FALSE}
# Knit from the project root rather than the notebook directory.
project_root <- if (file.exists("IFLS_Project.Rproj")) "." else ".."
knitr::opts_knit$set(root.dir = normalizePath(project_root, winslash = "/"))
knitr::opts_chunk$set(echo = TRUE, message = FALSE)
```

## 1. Prepare folders

Open `IFLS_Project.Rproj` first. Run the package installation script from the
Console once before knitting this notebook.

```{r folders}
source("02_scripts/00_setup_folders.R", local = TRUE)
```

## 2. Inspect the available Stata files

```{r inventory}
source_files <- sort(list.files(
  raw_dta_folder, pattern = "\\.dta$", ignore.case = TRUE,
  recursive = TRUE, full.names = TRUE
))

source_inventory <- data.frame(
  source_file = substring(source_files, nchar(raw_dta_folder) + 2L),
  size_mb = round(file.info(source_files)$size / 1024^2, 2)
)

knitr::kable(source_inventory, caption = "Original Stata files available locally")
```

## 3. Create the CSV copies explicitly

Run this command in the Console when your datasets are in place. This chunk is
disabled during knitting because a full conversion can take time.

```{r convert, eval=FALSE}
source("02_scripts/02_convert_all_dta_to_csv.R")
```

## 4. Load a dataset for later exploration

Use the `.dta` version in R when you want the original variable and value labels.
CSV copies are useful for exchanging data with other software. Read identifier
columns as character to avoid losing leading zeros. Here is an IFLS5 example;
change the relative filename if your extracted files are nested more deeply.

```{r load-example, eval=FALSE}
roster <- haven::read_dta(
  file.path(raw_dta_folder, "ifls5", "household", "bk_ar1.dta")
)
```
